title: Tor amplitude of a pro-etale complex
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme and $A$ a commutative ring, with the small pro-etale site $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], its constant sheaf of rings $A_Y$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], the abelian category $\Mod(A_Y)$ of sheaves of $A_Y$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and its derived category $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)=D(\Mod(A_Y))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and let $a\leq b$ be integers. Say that $K$ has *Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$* if for every sheaf $M$ of $A_Y$-modules, regarded as a complex placed in degree zero, the cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] of the derived tensor product [def-weil-derived-tensor] satisfy

$$
 \mathcal H^i(K\otimes^L_A M)=0\qquad\text{for every }i\in\mathbf Z\setminus[a,b].
$$

Say that $K$ has *finite Tor amplitude* (finite tor dimension) if it has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ for some integers $a\leq b$.

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Section 21.46 'Tor dimension', Definition 21.46.1 (Tag 08FZ, label definition-tor-amplitude), (1) and (2), specialized to the ringed site $(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_Y)$; for modules over a ring, More on Algebra, Definition Tag 0652

lean.note: Section 1(B), exact existing-interface repair. The module Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.CoefficientProEtaleTorAmplitude publicly imports the old module Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtaleTorAmplitude and retains its declarations AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.HasProEtaleTorAmplitude and AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.HasFiniteProEtaleTorAmplitude, while also exposing CategoryTheory.HasCoefficientModelTorAmplitude, AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.HasCoefficientProEtaleTorAmplitude, and AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.HasFiniteCoefficientProEtaleTorAmplitude. HasProEtaleTorAmplitude is confined to A : Type t and the ULift constant ring on the original Scheme.{t} site; it cannot accept the coefficient-sized constant-ring derived objects used by constructibleComparison. The coefficient-sized predicates are the same universal K-flat Tor tests on the equivalent small sites, with independent scheme and coefficient sizes; the finite variant requires a single ordered interval. No notion or tensor product is redefined.
